reviewer_independence: different subagent; exact input SHA audit and fresh Synopsys VCS compile/run

independent_replay.note: The testbench is deterministic; changing the seed demonstrates replayability, not additional random coverage.

recurrence_audit.formula: issue[i]=max(issue[i-1]+1, issue[i-8]+4, issue[i-(6*B)]+4) when each predecessor exists
recurrence_audit.safety_reason: A reused context request can issue on the prior response-accept edge; the prior skid commits one cycle later, while the new response cannot arrive until four cycles later.
recurrence_audit.scope: fixed L4/II1/O8, always-ready request/result/done, oldest-generation response

p1_findings: The cross-module reference is M218 output, not an independent arithmetic golden model; static signed-tree review reduces but does not eliminate shared-bug risk.
The testbench contains no randomized stimulus or stalls, so the alternate random seed is coverage-neutral.
At L=4, O=8 and 6*B>=6, both the outstanding and same-context recurrence terms are nonbinding; all observed issue spacing is II=1.
Only oldest-generation responses and permanently-ready request/result/done interfaces are covered; arbitrary out-of-order responses and backpressure are outside M220.
The -128/+127 corner exercises banks 0 and 1 only and is not an Acc24 overflow-boundary campaign.
M218 and M219 use separate but identically configured memory models and different response widths; M220 does not establish a physical shared-memory macro implementation.
The printed small-token completion cycles include fixed result drain and must not recalibrate or replace the frozen-H67 aggregate.
